Part 8: Microservice Usage

Service Boundary Interview Scenarios

Q: Merge payment-svc and ledger-svc?

A: No — different consistency models, PCI/audit boundaries, scale profiles (10K write vs batch post). Integrate via PaymentCompleted event + idempotent consumer. Exception: early startup monolith — strangler split later (Lesson 45).

Q: Sync ledger for strong consistency?

A: User-facing COMPLETED on payment aggregate after rail ACK; ledger eventual via event; EOD reconciliation authoritative; sync ledger couples availability — ADR rejects for corporate API SLO.

Q: Kafka vs RabbitMQ?

A: Kafka for high-throughput log, replay, multiple consumers (payment platform standard); Rabbit for task queue low volume — architect picks org standard MSK to avoid zoo of brokers.

Part 9: Architect Perspective

Incident Narratives (Gold in Interviews)

Duplicate PaymentCompleted

Symptom: ledger double entry same paymentId
Cause: consumer idempotency table missing; redeploy replay
Fix: UNIQUE(event_id), replay safe
Prevent: DLT monitoring, consumer contract test, STD-EVT-001

Consumer Lag During Deploy

Symptom: 500K lag after rolling update 09:00 NEFT peak
Cause: cooperative rebalance + slow startup + session timeout 10s
Fix: static membership, increase session.timeout.ms, deploy off-peak
Prevent: canary deploy, lag alert SEV-2

Saga Stuck in FUNDS_HELD

Symptom: payments stuck, account shows hold
Cause: rail adapter timeout, no timeout transition
Fix: saga sweeper job marks FAILED, compensate release
Prevent: timeout per state, dashboard stuck saga count

Model Answers — Staff / Architect

Q7 — Outbox pattern

A: Business row and outbox row inserted in single local DB transaction. Relay process reads PENDING outbox rows, publishes to Kafka with acks=all, marks SENT. Guarantees no lost events if DB commits. Avoids dual-write race where DB succeeds and Kafka fails. Debezium CDC alternative to polling relay. Payment-svc never publishes directly without outbox per STD-EVT-001.

Q10 — Dual write

A: Write DB then publish Kafka as separate operations without coordination. Crash between them → inconsistency (money committed, no event) or ghost event. Fix: outbox or transactional outbox via CDC. Interview: "Dual write is prohibited in our standards."

Q15 — Idempotency end-to-end

A: Client sends Idempotency-Key. Gateway passes through. payment-svc: Redis SET NX optional fast path; DB UNIQUE(tenant_id, key) authoritative in same tx as payment insert; return stored response on conflict. Kafka consumers dedupe by eventId table. Reconciliation catches any drift EOD. Retries safe at every layer.

Q18 — Partition key

A: Key = paymentId to preserve order of events for one payment lifecycle. If all events for tenant must be ordered (usually not), use tenantId — risk hot partition for large corporate tenant. 24 partitions → max 24 parallel consumers in one group. Scale partitions before peak with rebalance plan.

Q21 — Hot partition

A: One partition lag high while others low; producer rate skewed. Cause: bad key (all DEFAULT if null key). Fixes: salt key for analytics only topics; dedicated topic for whale tenant; increase partitions doesn't fix hot key if same key hash. Monitor per-partition lag metric.

Q27 — Consumer lag debug

A: Describe group lag per partition → identify hot vs global → check consumer count vs partitions → profile handler time → check DB/ downstream → review recent deploy rebalance → check poison message retry storm → thread dump if stuck → scale consumers or optimize handler → replay DLT after fix.

Q29 — Payment completion flow

A: payment-svc local tx: status COMPLETED + outbox PaymentCompleted. Relay → topic payment.completed key=paymentId acks=all. ledger-svc consumer idempotent by eventId posts entry. search-svc projects OpenSearch. notification-svc sends webhook. reconcile-svc increments counter. All async; user got 201 from sync path earlier. Failure: ledger lag OK; missing entry caught EOD batch.

  • [ ] I choose partition keys for payment + GPS
  • [ ] I narrate timeout stack numbers
  • [ ] I describe DLT + replay safely

Prerequisites: Lesson 42 (case studies) · Lessons 40–41 (HLD/LLD) · Lesson 48 (saga, outbox, Kafka) · Lessons 39, 44 (patterns, security) · Lessons 46–47 (Java/Spring depth for deep dives)

Part 1: Concept

What Is a System Design Interview?

A system design interview is a timed collaborative session (45–60 min) where you clarify requirements, estimate scale, draw architecture, deep-dive 2–3 hard problems, and discuss failures and trade-offs — while thinking aloud.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           SYSTEM DESIGN INTERVIEW — 45 MINUTE ARC                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                          │
│  0–5 min    Clarify scope, users, scale, constraints                     │
│  5–10 min   Back-of-envelope: QPS, storage, bandwidth                  │
│  10–20 min  High-level diagram + data flow + API sketch                  │
│  20–35 min  Deep dive #1 and #2 (interviewer-directed or you pick)       │
│  35–42 min  Failure modes, monitoring, security touch                    │
│  42–45 min  Summary, trade-offs, Phase 2                                 │
│                                                                          │
│  SCORED ON: communication, depth, trade-offs, pragmatism — not perfection│
│                                                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Interview Levels (Same Prompt, Different Bar)

Level Expectation on "Design payment API"
Senior Solid boxes, REST, DB, basic scale
Staff Idempotency, saga, failure paths, numbers
Solution Architect NFRs, compliance, migration, cost, org trade-offs
Principal Multi-year evolution, platform standards, risk register

Your target (9+ years → Solution Architect): Staff depth plus stakeholder and compliance narration.

Frameworks (Use One Fluently)

Framework Steps Best for
RESHADE (L42) Requirements, Estimation, Storage, High-level, API, Deep dive, Evolution General SD
BREAD (L45) Business, Requirements, Enterprise, Architecture, Delivery Solution architect prompts
RADIO (alternative) Requirements, Architecture, Data model, Interface, Optimizations Product-heavy

Pick RESHADE for most loops; add BREAD opening if prompt is enterprise/conglomerate.

Part 2: Why It Exists

Why Companies Use System Design Interviews

Coding tests:     Can you implement?
System design:    Can you build what 20 engineers run for 5 years?
Architect loop:   Can you align business, compliance, and boxes?

What Interviewers Actually Score (Hidden Rubric)

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              INTERVIEWER SCORECARD (TYPICAL)                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Communication (25%)  — structured, checks assumptions           │
│  Requirements (15%)   — functional + NFR + out of scope          │
│  High-level (20%)    — coherent diagram, clear boundaries        │
│  Deep dive (25%)     — idempotency, scale, consistency real depth│
│  Trade-offs (15%)    — alternatives named, justified choice      │
│                                                                  │
│  RED FLAGS: no questions, one DB, buzzwords, no failures, no nums│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Why Your Background Wins

Banking + logistics + transportation = money path + high write GPS + seat inventory + hybrid legacy. Use authentic domain stories — interviewers prefer real trade-offs over generic "Twitter clone."

Part 3: Internal Working

Phase 0: Clarification Script (First 5 Minutes)

Never draw before clarifying. Template:

"Before I design, I'd like to confirm a few things:

1. Who are the users — corporate API clients, retail mobile, internal ops?
2. Scale — daily volume and peak TPS if you have a target?
3. Consistency — must ledger be synchronous or eventual with reconciliation?
4. Geography — single region or multi-region DR?
5. Out of scope — search, analytics, admin UI?

I'll assume [state assumptions] unless you prefer otherwise."

Assumption Defaults (When Interviewer Says "You Decide")

Dimension Safe default (banking) Say aloud
Peak TPS 10K write "I'll design for 10K peak"
Read/write 10:1 read "100K read/s if needed"
Latency p95 500 ms initiate
Durability No lost payments
Ledger Eventual + EOD reconcile
Region Single primary + DR Phase 2
Multi-tenant Yes, tenant_id everywhere

Phase 1: Estimation (5 Minutes — Verbal Math)

Mental Math Shortcuts

1 day ≈ 100K seconds (86400 — round down for headroom)
1M requests/day ≈ 10 QPS average (1M/100K)
Peak factor 10× → 1M/day ≈ 100 QPS peak (NOT 10K — clarify!)

10M payments/day → 100 avg → 1000 peak (10×)
If interviewer says 10K TPS peak → ~1B/day order of magnitude

Storage:
  1 row ≈ 1 KB JSON payment → 1M rows/day × 365 × 5yr ≈ 1.8 TB raw
  + indexes ×2–3 → plan 5–10 TB with partition/archive

Estimation Table Template (Write on Board)

Metric Calculation Result
Peak write QPS given 10K
Ingress bandwidth 10K × 3 KB ~30 MB/s
DB write 10K × ~800 B + indexes ~15–20 MB/s
Kafka 10K evt × ~500 B ~5 MB/s
Pods 10K / 400 per pod ~25 pods + HPA

Architect bonus: "Production validates with k6; these are order-of-magnitude for sizing."

Phase 2: High-Level Design (10 Minutes)

Diagram Discipline

RULE 1: Left-to-right: clients → edge → services → data → async
RULE 2: Label sync (solid) vs async (dashed)
RULE 3: Name 5–8 boxes max on first pass — not 25 microservices
RULE 4: Show ONE primary write path bolded
RULE 5: DB per service — draw separate cylinders

Minimal Payment Hub First Pass

[Clients] → [WAF/ALB] → [API Gateway]
              → [payment-svc] ─sync─→ [account-svc], [fraud-svc]
                    │
                    ├─ [Aurora payment DB + outbox]
                    └─ dashed → [Kafka] → [ledger], [search], [notify]

API Sketch (2 endpoints enough)

POST /v1/payments     Idempotency-Key, 201 + paymentId
GET  /v1/payments/{id} status, amount, rail, timestamps

Phase 3: Deep Dives — Pick 2, Not 10

Deep Dive Menu (Payment)

Topic When interviewer probes Time
Idempotency Always for payment POST 8 min
Saga + outbox Money flow 8 min
Partition / scale 10K TPS 7 min
Reconciliation Banking 6 min
Search CQRS "Search by beneficiary" 6 min
Multi-tenant SaaS 5 min
Security / PCI Architect loop 6 min

Strategy: After HLD say: "I can deep-dive idempotency and saga/outbox, or scaling and Kafka — which is more useful?" Shows control.

Deep Dive #1 Script — Idempotency

1. Client sends Idempotency-Key header (UUID)
2. Gateway passes through
3. payment-svc: Redis SET NX (optional fast path, TTL 24h)
4. Authoritative: INSERT payment UNIQUE(tenant_id, idempotency_key)
5. Same request body hash optional — reject key reuse with different body (422)
6. On duplicate: return 200/201 with same paymentId + status
7. Survives Redis loss — DB is source of truth
8. Kafka consumers: separate eventId dedup table

Deep Dive #2 Script — Saga + Outbox

1. Reject XA across account and payment
2. Orchestrator in payment-svc, state table
3. Steps: validate → fraud (sync fail closed) → hold (sync account) → rail → COMPLETED
4. Each local transition: @Transactional payment row + outbox same commit
5. Relay publishes PaymentCompleted — ledger async
6. Failure after hold: compensate release — idempotent release API
7. Stuck saga sweeper job + ops dashboard
8. EOD reconciliation authoritative for money

Phase 4: Failures + Evolution (Last 8 Minutes)

Failure Table (Always Prepare 3)

Failure User impact Mitigation
fraud-svc down 503, no new payments Fail closed, alert, no bypass
account-svc slow Timeout → 503 or retry idempotent Bulkhead, circuit breaker
Kafka lag Status OK; ledger delayed Lag alert, scale consumers
AZ loss Brief 503 Multi-AZ EKS, Aurora failover
Duplicate client retry Same paymentId Idempotency

Phase 2 (Evolution) — 30 Seconds

"Phase 2: active-passive DR region, real-time fraud ML async,
 SWIFT rail adapter, read replica for reporting — not MVP."

│ TOP:     Requirements box (3 bullets functional, 3 NFR)        │
│ LEFT:    Actors / clients                                       │
│ CENTER:  Service diagram (main real estate)                     │

Interviewer Interrupt Handling

Interrupt: "What if Redis dies?"
GOOD: "Idempotency falls back to DB UNIQUE — slight latency increase, correctness preserved"
BAD:  panic and redraw entire diagram

Interrupt: "Isn't microservices overkill?"
GOOD: "For 100 TPS monolith fine; at 10K with separate UPI/NEFT release cadence, bounded services pay off"

Part 5: Performance Analysis

Estimation Drill Bank (Practice Aloud)

Drill 1 — URL Shortener (Warm-Up)

100M URLs/month create, 10:1 read
Write: 100M/(30×100K) ≈ 33 QPS avg → 330 peak
Read: 3300 QPS peak
Storage: 100M × 500B/month × 12 × 5yr — estimate TB, use base62 key 7 chars
Cache: 80/20 — Redis for hot reads

Drill 2 — Payment 10K TPS

Given peak 10K write (already peak — don't multiply again)
Aurora: need load test; ~25–30 app pods at 400 TPS each
Kafka: 24 partitions, 3 brokers, acks=all
Redis: idempotency 10K SET/s — cluster mode

Drill 3 — GPS 500K points/min (Logistics)

500K/60 ≈ 8.3K writes/s
100 B/point → 830 KB/s ingest
Kafka partitions by shipmentId
Redis latest + Cassandra history (Lesson 42-B)
Read 50K viewers — WebSocket fanout separate scaling

Drill 4 — Train seat booking festival

500 TPS booking writes, hot train coach contention
Optimistic lock @Version, return 409 retry
Schedule reads cached CDN/static + Redis

Part 6: Code Examples

Example 1: Opening Clarification (Payment — Full Script)

"I'm designing a corporate payment initiation API for B2B clients.

Assumptions unless you correct me:
- Peak 10K TPS initiate, p95 500ms
- Maker-checker for corporate; not designing branch UI today
- Ledger posting eventual via events; EOD reconciliation required
- Single region AWS with DR as Phase 2
- Out of scope: SWIFT, FX, mobile retail

Does that match what you want me to focus on?"

Example 2: Trade-Off Narration (Sync vs Async Ledger)

"Option A: synchronous ledger post — strong consistency, user waits,
coupled availability if ledger down after rail success.

Option B: async via outbox — meets 500ms SLO, industry norm for channels,
requires reconciliation control.

Given corporate API SLO and hybrid core, I choose B with idempotent ledger
consumer and nightly three-way match. We can add sync ledger for a
premium tier in Phase 2 if product requires it."

Example 3: Idempotency Schema (Whiteboard SQL)

CREATE TABLE payments (
  payment_id       UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id        VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  idempotency_key  VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  amount           NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL,
  status           VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
  created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key)
);

Example 4: Deep Dive Selection (Mid-Interview)

"I've covered the happy path and scale estimate.
The two riskiest areas are duplicate requests under retry and consistency
between payment and ledger without XA.
I'll deep-dive idempotency first, then outbox + saga — sound good?"

Example 5: Recovery When Stuck

"I'm weighing Cassandra vs Aurora for GPS history —
Cassandra wins on write volume and TTL; we'd lose cross-shipment SQL joins,
but analytics move to warehouse. I'll proceed with Cassandra for hot path
unless you want relational reporting in scope."

Part 8: Microservice Usage

When to Propose Microservices in Interview

SAY microservices when:
  - Interviewer gave multi-team / multi-rail / 10K TPS
  - Clear contexts: payment, account, fraud, ledger

START simpler when:
  - "Small startup MVP 100 QPS" → modular monolith + Postgres OK
  - Then: "I'd split at X TPS or Y team size"

Architect: always DB-per-service once you draw multiple services

Box Count Guidance

45 min interview sweet spot:
  Gateway, 1 orchestrator, 2–3 sync deps, 1 DB, Kafka, 2–3 async consumers
Not: 15 named microservices without grouping ("payment domain services")

Staff vs Solution Architect — Same Question, Extra Layers

Prompt: Design payment platform.

Staff ends at Solution Architect adds
Saga, outbox, 10K math Maker-checker, audit 7yr, PCI tokenization
Kafka, Redis Hybrid core ACL, migration strangler mention
Fail closed fraud STRIDE one-liner, fail-closed STD
HPA, partitions FinOps order of magnitude, ARB gate mention

Executive Sound Bite (Last 30 Sec)

"In summary: API Gateway with OAuth2, payment orchestrator with saga and
outbox, sync validate/fraud/hold, async ledger, idempotent throughout,
Aurora and Kafka sized for 10K TPS, fail closed on risk, reconciliation
EOD. Phase 2 DR and SWIFT. Primary risks: hybrid core latency and
operational saga recovery — mitigated by sweeper job and batch reconcile."

Part 12: Interview Questions

Meta (About the Interview)

  1. How do you structure 45 minutes?
  2. What if you don't know the technology they ask for?
  3. How deep on CAP theorem?
  4. Draw diagrams or talk? Both?

Practice Prompts — Self-Test

  1. Design corporate payment API 10K TPS.
  2. Design URL shortener like bit.ly.
  3. Design real-time logistics tracking.
  4. Design train ticket booking for festival peak.
  5. Design distributed rate limiter for API gateway.
  6. Design notification system for bank alerts.
  7. Design YouTube / video upload. (stretch)
  8. Design Twitter feed. (stretch)

Interviewer Probe Questions (During SD)

  1. Why Kafka not RabbitMQ?
  2. Why not one database?
  3. Duplicate POST — walk through.
  4. Partition count 24 — why?
  5. Multi-region active-active?
  6. How monitor health?
  7. Cost drivers?
  8. What did you defer and why?

Model Answers

Q1 — Structure 45 minutes

A: 5 clarify, 5 estimate, 10 HLD diagram + APIs, 15 two deep dives (idempotency + saga for payment), 5 failures, 3 evolution, 2 summary. Check in every 10 min. Leave buffer for interviewer probes.

Q5 — Payment 10K (Outline)

A: Clarify corporate, maker-checker, eventual ledger. Estimate 25 pods, Aurora, MSK 24 partitions. Gateway OAuth2 → payment-svc orchestrator → sync account/fraud fail closed → Aurora+outbox → Kafka → ledger/search. Deep dive idempotency Redis+UNIQUE and outbox saga compensate. Failures fraud down 503, Kafka lag reconcile. Phase 2 DR. Trade-offs narrated sync vs async ledger.

Q6 — URL Shortener

A: Clarify read-heavy 100:1, 100M new/month. Base62 7-char key or hash collision handling. POST create → hash → SQL/NoSQL store. GET redirect → Redis cache 80/20 → DB. CDN optional. Scale reads with cache cluster. Deep dive: key generation (counter vs random collision), cache invalidation. Not payment — show simpler consistency.

Q17 — Multi-region active-active payments

A: Reject Phase 1 for payments — conflict resolution on balance hard, regulatory data residency. Active-passive DR: Aurora global failover or restore RPO 15min, MSK MM2 optional. Mention CAP: choose CP for money in single primary. Architect credibility.

Q4 — Don't know technology

A: "I haven't operated Cassandra in prod, but for time-series GPS I'd use wide-column or TSDB for write scale and TTL — similar to Cassandra properties: partition key, eventual consistency, tunable replication. I'd validate with POC and align to org standards."

Part 13: Common Mistakes

# Mistake Recovery
1 No clarifying questions Pause: "Let me confirm scale…"
2 Jump to Kafka immediately Requirements first
3 Single MySQL for all Split DB per service
4 10 deep dives shallow "I'll pick two"
5 No numbers Round on board even rough
6 Ignore failures Add table when reminded
7 Draw-only silence Narrate every box
8 Microservices for 50 QPS Monolith OK
9 Perfectionism one box Move on, return if time
10 Argue interviewer "Good point — I'd adjust to…"

Part 14: Best Practices

  1. Clarify 5 min — write assumptions visible
  2. Estimate aloud — even wrong math corrected beats silence
  3. One diagram pass — iterate, don't restart
  4. Two deep dives — ask interviewer preference
  5. Trade-off template — A vs B, choose X because Y
  6. Failures always three — fraud, dependency, AZ/partition
  7. Phase 2 line — shows scope control
  8. Domain authenticity — banking/logistics from your CV
  9. Timed mocks — 45 min strict weekly
  10. Record yourself — filler words, pace, structure

Part 1: Concept

What Is a Solution Architect Interview Loop?

A Solution Architect interview loop is a multi-round evaluation (typically 4–6 sessions over 1–2 days) testing system design, architecture judgment, stakeholder communication, leadership, and domain credibility — not coding speed alone.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           TYPICAL SOLUTION ARCHITECT LOOP (5–6 ROUNDS)                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                          │
│  R1  Recruiter / HM screen     — scope, comp, role fit                   │
│  R2  System design (60 min)    — payment / platform design (Lesson 49)   │
│  R3  Architecture deep-dive    — trade-offs, ADR, migration, governance  │
│  R4  Domain + behavioral       — STAR stories, conflict, influence       │
│  R5  Executive / peer          — business case, roadmap, "why you"       │

Part 2: Why It Exists

Why Solution Architect Loops Differ from Senior Loops

Senior loop:     "Can you build payment-svc?"
Architect loop:  "Can you prevent 5 teams building 5 payment platforms,
                  get funding for platform Phase 0, and explain PCI scope
                  to audit without an engineer in the room?"

What Gets Candidates Rejected at Architect Level

Rejection reason What they needed
Brilliant diagram, no business link Tie to OKR, cost, risk
Cannot push back politely Structured trade-off, not "no"
No legacy/hybrid empathy Strangler, ACL, phased gates
Ivory tower patterns Fitness functions + squad embed
Weak behavioral STAR with metrics
Over-engineer every answer Phase 1 MVP + Phase 2

Your Competitive Edge

9+ years Java/Spring/Kafka/AWS + banking + logistics + transportation
= rare combination for SA roles in BFSI and supply chain digital

You are not "learning architecture from YouTube"
You are naming patterns you should have lived — authentically

Part 3: Internal Working

The ARCH Loop Framework (Answer Structure)

For any architect round:

A — Anchor on business outcome first
R — Requirements and constraints (regulatory, time, budget)
C — Core architecture decision with trade-off
H — How delivered / governed (ARB, ADR, phases)

Round-by-Round Playbook

R1 — Hiring Manager Screen (30 min)

They assess: level, motivation, comp alignment, communication

Your opener:

"I'm a Java technical lead with 9+ years in banking payments and logistics
platforms — Spring, Kafka, AWS, K8s. I'm moving to Solution Architect because
I've been owning HLD, migration roadmaps, and cross-team standards, and I want
that as my primary role: reference architecture, ARB, and business-aligned
technical strategy — not only sprint delivery."

Expected questions:

Question Answer angle
Why architect now? Already doing HLD, governance, migration — formalize scope
Why leave? Growth ceiling as TL; want enterprise impact
Comp expectations? Research market; flexible on level Staff/SA
On-site hybrid? Prepared

R2 — System Design (60 min) — Lesson 49 Execution

Prompt (common): Design a corporate payment platform for 10K TPS.

Use RESHADE. Differentiator at SA level — close with executive summary (Lesson 49).

Interviewer interrupts — mock script:

INTERVIEWER: "Why not put ledger in same database as payment?"
YOU: "Coupling release cycles and PCI/audit scope. Separate ledger-svc with
async outbox gives independent scale and clear ownership. Hybrid period uses
reconciliation — I've run that in core migration. Short-term exception possible
with expiry, not target state. STD-DATA-001 in our catalog enforced DB-per-service."

R3 — Architecture Deep-Dive (45–60 min)

Topics:

  • ADR example you " wrote"
  • Strangler migration timeline
  • Kafka vs sync for ledger
  • Governance: ARB tier, fitness functions
  • Security: fail-closed fraud, PCI tokenization
  • Incident you drove to systemic fix

Mock Q&A:

INTERVIEWER: "Walk me through an ADR you disagreed with but accepted."
YOU (STAR-ARCH):
  Situation: Squad wanted sync ledger for 'simplicity'
  Task: ARB chair — decide without blocking release
  Action: Accepted with condition — 6-month metric review; mandatory reconciliation
          dashboard; ADR-027 documents async as standard with sync exception path
  Result: Sync path never met SLO; exception expired; team migrated to outbox
  Learning: Conditional approve + metrics beats hard no

R4 — Behavioral + Domain (45 min)

Use STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) — 2 min max per story.

Story bank mapped to YOUR domains:

Theme Story seed (customize with real projects)
Influence without authority Convinced 3 squads to adopt Idempotency-Key standard
Conflict Product wanted skip fraud for deadline — fail-closed ADR
Failure Duplicate payment incident → STD + fitness test
Migration Oracle→AWS strangler, ACL, 18-month phases
Scale Kafka lag during peak NEFT — rebalance + deploy window
Mentoring Elevated TL to own LLD review checklist
Stakeholder Explained PCI scope to non-technical audit

R5 — Executive / Peer (30–45 min)

They assess: business fluency, executive presence, strategic fit

Mock prompt:

CPO: "We have ₹50 crore and 12 months. Payment hub or logistics command
center first — you pick one."

Model answer:

"I'd prioritize payment hub if revenue and regulatory exposure dominate —
duplicate payment risk and corporate API revenue are existential. Logistics
command center improves SLA and shipper retention but rarely carries PCI
and settlement risk.

Payment hub Phase 0–1 in 6 months delivers corporate API on reference
architecture; logistics can consume shared MSK and Gateway platform built
in Phase 0 — platform investment isn't wasted.

I'd show board: payment ROI in fee revenue + audit risk reduction; logistics
follows on same EKS/MSK footprint in months 7–12.

If your OKR is shipper NPS this quarter, I'd flip — but I'd surface payment
reconciliation debt as risk register item."

R6 — Bar Raiser (60 min)

Deep fundamentals from Lessons 46–48 + judgment:

- HashMap + concurrent payment cache
- @Transactional saga boundary
- Kafka at-least-once + idempotency
- CAP on multi-region payments — reject active-active Phase 1
- "Tell me about a time you were wrong"

Judgment question:

INTERVIEWER: "Team shipped shared database despite your objection."
YOU: "Document exception EXC with expiry and compensating controls; don't
      undermine in hallway. Escalate if no expiry. Post-incident if audit
      fails — architecture is governance not heroics. I've learned public
      I-told-you-so destroys ARB credibility."

Part 6: Code Examples

Example 1: Elevator Pitch (60 Seconds)

"I'm a hands-on architect candidate with nine years building Java payment
and logistics systems on Spring, Kafka, and AWS. I've led microservice
migrations from core Oracle, defined idempotency and outbox standards,
and partnered with security on PCI scope reduction. I design for 10K TPS
with saga and reconciliation — not theoretical slides. I'm looking to
own reference architecture and ARB for a payment or supply-chain platform
while staying technical enough to review LLDs and fitness functions."

Example 2: Business Case Slide (Verbal)

PROBLEM: 3 payment stacks, 18-month feature duplication, reconciliation gaps
SOLUTION: Unified hub on AWS — strangler from core
INVESTMENT: ₹XX cr / 18 mo — platform + 2 stream teams
RETURN: 40% faster corporate features; audit finding closure; 10K TPS ready
RISK: Hybrid complexity — mitigated phased gates + EOD reconcile
ASK: Approve Phase 0 platform + Phase 1 corporate go-live

Example 3: 30/60/90 Day Plan

DAYS 1–30 (LISTEN):
  - Meet squad leads, product, security, ops
  - Read existing HLD, ADR index, incident history
  - Shadow ARB; map tech debt register
  - Deliver: current-state assessment + top 5 risks (no rewrites yet)

DAYS 31–60 (ALIGN):
  - Publish reference architecture v0.9 draft
  - Run 2 office hours; review 1 critical HLD
  - Propose 3 fitness functions for CI
  - Align CPO on Phase 1 scope

DAYS 61–90 (EXECUTE):
  - ARB approve reference arch v1.0
  - Gate Phase 1 corporate API with load test criteria
  - Close or expire one major exception (e.g., shared legacy read)
  - Metrics dashboard: TPS, recon drift, deployment frequency

Example 4: Conflict — Shared DB Pushback

PRODUCT: "Shared DB saves 6 weeks — we'll split later."

YOU: "I hear the deadline pressure. Shared DB couples deploys and expands
PCI scope — 6 weeks now often becomes 18 months of debt. Options:
  A) 6-week ACL read service over legacy — no write coupling
  B) Time-boxed exception with read-only user, expires June, debt ticket funded Q2
  C) Descope beneficiary search from MVP — reduces need for join

I recommend B with written exception if A isn't staffed. I won't approve
silent shared write access."

Example 5: Closing Questions (Impress)

1. "What architecture decision from last year would you redo — and why?"
2. "How does ARB interact with product prioritization when debt competes with features?"
3. "What does success look like for this role at 12 months — measurable?"
4. "Biggest hybrid legacy pain I should expect in first 90 days?"

Avoid: "What are your perks?" as only question.

Part 12: Interview Questions

Behavioral (Prepare STAR)

  1. Tell me about a time you influenced without authority.
  2. Disagreement with product on deadline vs quality?
  3. Failed migration or rollout — what happened?
  4. Mentored someone to architect thinking?
  5. Explained technical trade-off to executive?
  6. Time you were wrong — publicly?
  7. Handled security vs velocity conflict?
  8. Prioritized tech debt vs feature?
  9. Worked with legacy team hostile to cloud?
  10. Largest system you architected end-to-end?

Architect Judgment

  1. Build vs buy payment engine?
  2. Monolith rewrite or strangler?
  3. When approve architecture exception?
  4. Multi-region payments day one?
  5. How measure architect success?

Meta / Closing

  1. Why Solution Architect vs Staff?
  2. What do you want in 3 years?
  3. Questions for us?

Model Answers — Selected

Q1 — Influence without authority

A: Situation: Three squads, three idempotency implementations, duplicate payment incident. Task: No direct reports outside my team. Action: Drafted STD-PAY-003, built reference filter + ArchUnit rule, ran 2 lunch demos, got platform team to enforce in parent POM; ARB made mandatory. Result: Zero duplicate idempotency-class incidents next 4 quarters; adopted as org standard. Lesson: standards + automation beat emails.

Q11 — Build vs buy payment engine

A: Build orchestration — core IP, maker-checker, reconciliation to internal core, audit. Buy commodity: SMS, KYC OCR, optional fraud rules engine with ACL. SaaS full stack only if exit cost and data residency acceptable — rarely for tier-1 corporate banking. 5-year TCO and regulatory control favor build hub on reference arch (Lesson 43 rubric).

Q15 — Measure architect success

A: hub migration %, deployment frequency without recon drift, mean time to approve T2 ARB, exception count trending down, SLO error budget, cost per transaction trend, squad satisfaction with templates — not lines of code I wrote.

Q16 — SA vs Staff

A: Staff optimizes technical excellence in domain; SA optimizes business outcomes across domains with governance. I've been doing both; title SA matches stakeholder-facing scope I want while staying hands-on on LLD and fitness functions.
